skill.name: product-metrics
skill.description: Find the Product Metrics workflow for your store platform and ad channel. Route server-side conversion tracking, customer matching, profit bidding, and product segmentation tasks across Google Ads, Meta, and ChatGPT Ads.
skill.summary: Find the right Product Metrics workflow and check what is already configured.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: Most scanner hits are Markdown labels or documentation links, and none of the three reconnaissance alerts show host or network probing. The skill does direct CLI and remote service use, including scoped order reads and installation of an unpinned companion skill. The instructions leave gaps in credential handling, approval for some account changes, and validation of browser handoffs.

remediation.issue: Companion skill installation is not pinned or approval-gated.
remediation.suggestion: Default to reviewed local instructions. Before installation, show the exact skill and pinned revisions of the installer and skill source, then require explicit approval.

remediation.issue: The assistant is instructed to accept and pass raw integration credentials.
remediation.suggestion: Use a vendor-managed secret entry form or a secret reference. Keep raw keys and tokens out of chat, tool arguments, and process arguments.

remediation.issue: Some account changes lack an explicit approval step.
remediation.suggestion: Before each change, show the action and target account and wait for approval. Reuse the original idempotency key when retrying the same approved write.

remediation.issue: Browser handoffs forward URLs returned by tools without requiring validation.
remediation.suggestion: Verify the HTTPS origin against the expected service or confirmed store admin domain. Do not forward unexpected URLs or direct users to paste setup tokens there.

remediation.issue: Order lookups can return confidential business data.
remediation.suggestion: Confirm the storefront scope before reading orders and retrieve only the fields needed. Prefer aggregate results or a designated test order when possible.

finding_verdicts.reason: The backticks are Markdown, but the rule explicitly directs the assistant to run CLI status and help commands, invoking a local executable.
The assistant is told to execute a setup status command and repeat it with company and property identifiers. Its output can include account setup details.
The backticks mark identifier names. The line says to obtain them from earlier results and contains no shell command.
The rule directs the assistant to run CLI or MCP writes and retry failures. Idempotency can reduce duplicate writes but does not prevent account changes.
The inline text describes tool response values. The browser and plugin actions are assigned to the user, not executed through those backticks.
The assistant is directed to run order list and detail commands. These scoped reads expose order margins and customer status to the assistant.
The rule offers an actual CLI or MCP lookup to identify the store platform. Asking the user instead avoids that account lookup.
The highlighted strings are a placeholder and permitted platform names for skill selection, not executable commands.
The tracking row maps ad channels to companion skill names. The table entries do not execute commands.
The entries are skill identifiers for enhanced conversions and matching, not commands or requests to execute them.
The Google Ads Customer Match entry names a companion skill. It does not run a command or upload a list.
The new customer bidding row lists skill names for supported channels without invoking a command.
The returning customer bidding row contains companion skill names, not executable bid changes.
The table uses inline code to label profit and revenue bidding skills. The names are not run by a shell.
The lifetime value bidding row names skills for three channels without providing a shell invocation.
The tracking setup entry names a workflow and describes its scope. It does not execute setup commands.
The backticks label the Google Ads connection skill. The row itself does not initiate a connection.
The line names a read-only tracking check skill. It does not contain a test order lookup command.
The profit bidding entry describes a companion skill rather than invoking an executable.
The line names an ad performance analysis skill and sample business questions. It contains no shell command.
The product segment check is a skill name in the table, not a command that inspects segment data.
The line describes a product profitability workflow and its expected data. It does not execute an analysis command.
The segmentation setup entry is a skill label. The row describes possible changes after confirmation but does not run them.
The campaign structure check is a routing label for a read-only workflow, not a shell instruction.
The stock and returns entry names a skill and its reporting scope. It does not fetch inventory or returns itself.
The backticks label the general new customer bidding skill. The row contains no executable invocation.
The returning customer bidding entry names a workflow rather than a command that changes ad settings.
The lifetime value bidding entry identifies a companion skill. The inline label has no execution behavior.
The skill directs the assistant to run an unpinned npx installer for a missing companion skill. There is no required approval or integrity check.
The backticks mark fallback skill names for ChatGPT Ads, not shell commands.
The inline literal is an MCP URL, not a shell command. The remote connection is covered by the network finding.
The highlighted values are a directory name and a file extension. The documentation fallback does not specify a shell command.
The URL is a documentation pointer in front matter. The metadata does not initiate a request or send data.
The matched URLs point to the public documentation and its index. Neither is an operational destination for the order signals described in the same paragraph.
The rule directs the assistant to use a remote MCP endpoint when the CLI is unavailable. Tool execution can send account parameters to that service.
The URL points to a longer explanation of the CLI rules. The line does not request an operational connection or data transfer.
The URL links to custom store documentation, not to the receiving webhook. The line does not send orders to that documentation URL.

The matched URL is a costs documentation page. It is not the destination of the profit data described in the sentence.
The link explains consent handling. It is not a tracking endpoint and the line does not direct visitor data to it.
The line directs users to connect a remote MCP server for campaign and product analysis. Queries can expose account context to the service.
The paragraph describes advertising and ecommerce analytics. It does not enumerate hosts, networks, or system configuration.
The commands retrieve business orders within a supplied company and storefront scope. They do not inspect host or network resources.
The line describes read-only campaign performance analysis. The referenced figures concern ad results, not system discovery.

semantic_findings.title: Raw Integration Credentials Passed Through the Assistant
semantic_findings.description: The secret rule allows the assistant to receive specific merchant API credentials and pass them directly to a command. Chat, tool telemetry, or process arguments may retain the values despite the instruction not to log them.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The rule explicitly allows raw API keys and tokens to pass through the assistant. It does not require a secret input channel or a credential reference.

semantic_findings.title: Incomplete Approval for Account Changes
semantic_findings.description: The workflow requires approval for deletes and segmentation changes, and reserves primary conversion selection for the user. It does not require approval of the target and action before other setup writes, such as creating secondary conversion actions.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The write rule addresses retry behavior, while confirmation is specified only for selected actions. An idempotency key is not user authorization.

semantic_findings.title: Unvalidated Browser Handoffs
semantic_findings.description: The assistant is told to direct the user to a URL returned by a tool without checking its origin. An unexpected destination could be presented as a legitimate setup page.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The handoff uses a response field and specifies no origin check. Whether the service separately validates returned URLs is not shown.

content.user_title: Find the Right Ecommerce Ad Tracking Workflow
content.value_statement: Ad tracking and bidding setup vary by store platform and ad channel. Product Metrics identifies the matching workflow and helps you distinguish completed setup from steps that still need attention.
actual_capabilities: Selects a companion workflow by task, store platform, and ad channel.
Reads Product Metrics setup status through the CLI or MCP and identifies steps that are already complete.
Separates assistant steps from store admin, browser, and advertising account steps that the user performs.
Looks up scoped orders to check margin and whether a customer is new or returning.
Routes campaign performance, product profitability, and Shopping or Performance Max segmentation reviews to companion skills.
limitations: Account lookups need an authorized Product Metrics connection and the correct store scope.
Detailed workflows live in separate skills or vendor documentation.
Selecting the conversion a campaign optimizes for remains a manual step.
Profit signals require complete order costs, and Customer Match lists are available only for Google Ads.

use_cases.title: Plan conversion tracking for a store
use_cases.description: Identify the workflow for your store platform and ad channel, then see which setup steps need your attention.

use_cases.title: Find the right profit bidding workflow
use_cases.description: Choose the relevant workflow for profit, revenue, or lifetime value bidding and check which tracking prerequisites are missing.

use_cases.title: Start a product profitability review
use_cases.description: Identify the workflow for finding products that lose money after ad spend and list the data needed for the review.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a tracking workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: My store uses Shopify and I advertise on Google Ads. Which Product Metrics workflow should I use for server-side conversion tracking? Recommend the workflow without installing anything.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: choose a setup workflow for a known store and channel.

prompt_templates.title: Check existing setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Check the Product Metrics setup status for this WooCommerce storefront and Meta account. List completed steps, the next manual step, and anything you could not verify. Do not make changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: resume setup in an authorized account.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a designated test order
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the approved company and storefront scope to check this test order. Report only its margin and whether the customer was new or returning. Do not show customer identifiers.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: verify an order signal without exposing unrelated records.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a profit and segmentation review
prompt_templates.prompt: Before we move Google Ads bidding to profit, identify the workflows for checking order costs, product losses, and Performance Max segment coverage. Separate read-only checks from proposed changes. Do not install skills or change settings.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: sequence a review across tracking, profitability, and campaign structure.

output_examples.input: I use Shopify and want to set up both server-side tracking and Advanced Matching for Meta.
output: Start with the Shopify workflow for the Meta Conversions API.
After server-side tracking is in place, use the Shopify workflow for Meta Advanced Matching.
Select the conversion your campaign uses in Meta yourself.

output_examples.input: How do I interpret a return on ad spend of 4.2 and a profit-based target of 100 percent?
output: A return on ad spend of 4.2 means 4.2 units of revenue for every unit of ad spend.
A profit-based target of 100 percent means profit equals ad spend. That is the break-even point.

best_practices: State the store platform, ad channel, and goal before choosing a workflow.
Check setup status and confirm the company and storefront scope before reading orders.
Review tracking, consent, and order costs before using profit as a bidding goal.
anti_patterns: Guessing a company, property, or storefront identifier.
Pasting API keys into chat or sharing full order records when a scoped result is enough.
Asking the assistant to make a conversion action primary or change campaign optimization directly.

faq.question: Which store platforms are covered?
faq.answer: The router lists Shopify, WooCommerce, Lightspeed eCom C-Series, Magento 2, Shopware 6, and Cloudflare Tracking. Vendor documentation also covers custom stores that send orders by webhook.

faq.question: Which advertising channels are covered?
faq.answer: The router covers Google Ads, Meta, and ChatGPT Ads. The available workflows vary by channel and task.

faq.question: Do I need to connect Product Metrics?
faq.answer: No connection is needed to choose a workflow if you know your store platform and channel. Live status and order checks need an authorized connection.

faq.question: What happens if a companion skill is missing?
faq.answer: The vendor provides documentation as an alternative. Review the source and approve any installation separately before adding a skill.

faq.question: What is the difference between POAS and ROAS?
faq.answer: POAS measures profit divided by ad spend. ROAS measures revenue divided by ad spend.

faq.question: Can the assistant switch my campaign to a new conversion?
faq.answer: No. The assistant can identify the steps and check the result, but you select the conversion in the advertising platform.
